# Rumbletect

> Rumbletect is a browser app that designs the continuous sound of jets, airliners, rockets, and volcanic eruptions from their physics. A scene places sources (jets, formations, airliners, rockets, salvos, eruption jets) on authored paths and microphones in 3D over real terrain and layered air, and renders what each microphone hears. It is a creative tool for sound design: a result is a plausible sound, not a reconstruction or a measurement, and levels are uncalibrated model values in pascals.

Rumbletect runs entirely in the browser, with no account and no server of its own. A source is a stream of short noise grains along its path, each with a position, an emission time, and a spectrum toward every direction; each grain travels to each microphone with its own delay, Doppler shift, and loss, and the microphone hears their sum. Long grains carry the sound below 20 Hz. Every part of the model is marked A (first principles), B (literature), or C (heuristic or synthetic). Rumbletect shares its place, terrain, air, propagation, and interface with Boomtect.

Exports are 32-bit float WAV at one full scale in pascals, recorded in the scene JSON; per-microphone files start at the same moment. A scene is JSON with `"format": "rumbletect.scene"` and opens again as a scene. A sound sent to Echotect is mono pressure without terrain echoes with a `tect.handoff` JSON: positions in metres east, north, and up from the place's geographic point, angles in compass degrees clockwise from north. The scene and handoff readers fill in missing fields with defaults, bring values into range, and never refuse an older or newer version.

Opened from each other, Boomtect and Rumbletect link their windows: they share the scene's place, terrain, air, ground, microphones, and render settings, each renders only its own emitters, and the microphones hear the sum, which the plots, levels, playback, and export use.

An agent can render without the browser: clone the repository and run `node tools/render.mjs <scene.json> <folder>` with Node 20 or later and no installed packages. A partial scene is enough; the folder gets one WAV per microphone and the filled scene, and stdout gives levels, length, and spectral shape so the result can be checked without listening. Start from the nearest file in `examples/` and change what the request names. With GPS coordinates in `place` and `"terrain": { "enabled": true }` the render loads the real terrain; `tools/mix.mjs` puts a Boomtect and a Rumbletect render of the same scene together in time, with each part as its own file.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/janne-s/Rumbletect/blob/main/README.md): what every control does, the export files, and the model table with sources and classes
- [Sounds from words](https://github.com/janne-s/Rumbletect/blob/main/README.md#sounds-from-words): Claude Desktop (`tect.mcpb`), Codex and ChatGPT desktop (`tect-openai.zip`), coding agents, writing a scene and what each change does to the sound, and the render command
- [Examples](https://github.com/janne-s/Rumbletect/tree/main/examples): starting scenes for requests
- [Live app](https://janne-s.github.io/Rumbletect/)

## Formats

- [Scene](https://github.com/janne-s/Rumbletect/blob/main/src/domain/scene.js): every parameter with its default and range
- [Handoff](https://github.com/janne-s/Rumbletect/blob/main/src/shared/domain/handoff.js): the `tect.handoff` format shared with Boomtect and Echotect
- [Constants](https://github.com/janne-s/Rumbletect/blob/main/src/domain/constants.js): the model's tuning values and limits

## Optional

- [Boomtect](https://janne-s.github.io/Boomtect/llms.txt): lightning, blasts, and sonic booms simulated from their physics
- [Echotect](https://janne-s.github.io/Echotect/llms.txt): echoes from buildings, streets, and terrain for a sound, including one sent from Rumbletect
